text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.66% today, extending a steep two-week decline of 7.4%. The core driver appears to be a broader unwinding of the refinery trade itself—a CNBC report on November 23rd explicitly stated that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating out of the sector after an extended rally. This pullback comes even as refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity utilization, so the sell-off reflects a shift in market appetite rather than operational weakness.

The timing also matters: the failed COP31 climate summit and mixed geopolitical signals in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, but no major supply disruption) created an environment where refinery stocks lost momentum. Oil prices remain relatively stable in the $89–$93 range, which should support refining margins, but that hasn't been enough to reverse sentiment as money moves elsewhere.
